title: LexiQL: Quantum Natural Language Processing on NISQ-era Machines
problem: Natural language processing on quantum computers is underexplored for NISQ-era devices. The challenge is performing text classification while managing noise and hardware limitations inherent in current quantum machines.
motivation: Advancing quantum hardware creates an opportunity to explore quantum natural language processing applications on near-term devices that could overcome classical limitations.
method: LexiQL converts text into quantum circuits by gradually feeding in the text data step-by-step—a technique called incremental data injection—rather than loading it all at once. It uses quantum circuits of varying depths: some shallow (with fewer quantum operations, making them more stable on noisy hardware) and some deeper (capable of more complex transformations). The training process accounts for errors that naturally occur in NISQ devices—today's quantum computers with limited capacity and high error rates. This mix of circuit designs is tuned to classify text effectively despite these hardware limitations.
key_novelty: LexiQL performs text classification by using incremental data injection and shallow quantum circuits specifically tuned to handle the noise limitations of current-generation quantum machines.
contributions: LEXIQL: a noise-aware QNLP technique for text classification on NISQ quantum machines
Incremental data injection approach for processing textual data in quantum circuits
Novel training methods combining shallow and expressible quantum circuits for NISQ performance
Extensive evaluation on Yelp, IMDB, Amazon, and synthetic datasets demonstrating effectiveness in noisy environments
